units.source_text: 白居易《庾楼晓望》诗云：“独凭朱槛立凌晨，山色初明水色新。

en.t: Bai Juyi's poem "Morning View from Yu Tower" says: "Alone, leaning on the vermilion railing, I stand at dawn; the mountains are just beginning to brighten, and the color of the water is fresh.

units.source_text: 竹雾晓笼衔岭月，风暖送过江春。

en.t: Morning mist among the bamboo veils the moon resting on the ridge; a warm wind carries spring across the river.

units.source_text: 子城阴处犹残雪，衙鼓声前未有尘。

en.t: In the shaded parts of the inner city, snow still lingers; before the office drum sounds, no dust has yet risen.

units.source_text: 三百年来庾楼上，曾经多少望乡人。”

en.t: For three hundred years, how many people longing for home have stood upon Yu Tower and gazed into the distance?"
